bounds: One untrusted env overlay drawn from four keys (GIT_PROXY_COMMAND, GIT_EXEC_PATH, the already blocked GIT_SSH_COMMAND, and the ordinary GIT_AUTHOR_NAME), each written at most once, and up to six steps drawn from: one overlay write, a git:// fetch, and an https fetch. The conformance script replays every generated step sequence through sanitizeSpawnEnv and a real `git ls-remote` child process against a closed loopback port, with each overlay key pointing at a planted script or directory that leaves a marker file if git runs it, and it requires every one of the 16 overlay subsets to reach both a git:// and an https fetch. The config-write gate (packages/agent isBlockedEnvKey, which imports the same set), the PATH/HOME baseline each spawn consumer restores, ssh:// transports and other blocked keys are not modeled. Under weak fairness of git fetches, every overlay write is eventually used by a git run that executes nothing planted. Explicit stuttering lets nobody run git, so the same claim without fairness must fail. No latency bound is proved.

assumptions: Every continuously enabled git fetch eventually runs (weak fairness). This checks that a git run after an overlay write uses the sanitized overlay and executes no planted helper, not how soon git runs.
No fetch fairness is assumed. Nobody may ever run git, so a temporal loop counterexample is required.
